passages.text: Three days after his arrival in the province, Festus went up from Caesarea to Jerusalem, where the chief priests and Jewish leaders presented their case against Paul. They urged Festus to grant them a concession against Paul by summoning him to Jerusalem, because they were preparing an ambush to kill him along the way.
passages.sermon:
Festus was the new governor of the province.
Three days after Festus arrived in the province, he went up from Caesarea to Jerusalem.
The chief priests and the Jewish leaders met with Festus in Jerusalem.
They presented their case against Paul to Festus.
They urged Festus to do them a favor against Paul.
They asked Festus to summon Paul to Jerusalem.
They were planning an ambush to kill Paul on the way.
passages.original: Φῆστος οὖν ἐπιβὰς τῇ ἐπαρχείᾳ μετὰ τρεῖς ἡμέρας ἀνέβη εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα ἀπὸ Καισαρείας ἐνεφάνισάν τε αὐτῷ οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ οἱ πρῶτοι τῶν Ἰουδαίων κατὰ τοῦ Παύλου καὶ παρεκάλουν αὐτὸν αἰτούμενοι χάριν κατ’ αὐτοῦ ὅπως μεταπέμψηται αὐτὸν εἰς Ἰερουσαλήμ ἐνέδραν ποιοῦντες ἀνελεῖν αὐτὸν κατὰ τὴν ὁδόν

passages.text: But Festus replied, “Paul is being held in Caesarea, and I myself am going there soon.
passages.sermon:
Festus was the new governor.
Festus spoke to the Jewish leaders.
Festus said that Paul was being kept in Caesarea.
Festus said he would go to Caesarea soon.
passages.original: Ὁ μὲν οὖν Φῆστος ἀπεκρίθη τηρεῖσθαι τὸν Παῦλον εἰς Καισάρειαν ἑαυτὸν δὲ μέλλειν ἐν τάχει ἐκπορεύεσθαι

passages.text: So if this man has done anything wrong, let some of your leaders come down with me and accuse him there.”
passages.sermon:
Festus was the Roman governor.
Festus spoke to the Jewish leaders.
He said, “Some of your leaders should come with me to Caesarea.
If Paul has done anything wrong, they can accuse him there.”
passages.original: Οἱ οὖν ἐν ὑμῖν φησίν Δυνατοὶ συνκαταβάντες εἴ τί ἐστιν ἐν τῷ ἀνδρὶ ἄτοπον κατηγορείτωσαν αὐτοῦ

passages.text: After spending no more than eight or ten days with them, Festus went down to Caesarea. The next day he sat on the judgment seat and ordered that Paul be brought in.
passages.sermon:
Festus was the Roman governor.
He stayed with the people for no more than eight or ten days.
Then Festus went down to Caesarea.
The next day, Festus sat on the judgment seat.
Festus ordered that Paul be brought in.
passages.original: Διατρίψας δὲ ἐν αὐτοῖς ἡμέρας οὐ πλείους ὀκτὼ ἢ δέκα καταβὰς εἰς Καισάρειαν τῇ ἐπαύριον καθίσας ἐπὶ τοῦ βήματος ἐκέλευσεν τὸν Παῦλον ἀχθῆναι

passages.text: When Paul arrived, the Jews who had come down from Jerusalem stood around him, bringing many serious charges that they could not prove.
passages.sermon:
Paul arrived.
Jews had come down from Jerusalem.
These Jews stood around Paul.
They brought many serious charges against him.
They could not prove these charges.
passages.original: παραγενομένου δὲ αὐτοῦ περιέστησαν αὐτὸν οἱ ἀπὸ Ἱεροσολύμων καταβεβηκότες Ἰουδαῖοι πολλὰ καὶ βαρέα αἰτιώματα καταφέροντες ἃ οὐκ ἴσχυον ἀποδεῖξαι

passages.text: Then Paul made his defense: “I have committed no offense against the law of the Jews or against the temple or against Caesar.”
passages.sermon:
Paul spoke in his own defense.
Paul said he had done nothing wrong.
He said he had not broken the law of the Jews.
He said he had not sinned against the temple.
He said he had not offended Caesar.
passages.original: Τοῦ Παύλου ἀπολογουμένου ὅτι Οὔτε εἰς τὸν νόμον τῶν Ἰουδαίων οὔτε εἰς τὸ ἱερὸν οὔτε εἰς Καίσαρά τι ἥμαρτον

passages.text: But Festus, wishing to do the Jews a favor, said to Paul, “Are you willing to go up to Jerusalem to stand trial before me on these charges?”
passages.sermon:
Festus was the Roman governor.
Festus wanted to please the Jews.
Festus spoke to Paul.
Festus asked Paul a question.
Festus said, “Do you want to go up to Jerusalem?”
Festus said, “Will you be judged there by me on these charges?”
passages.original: Ὁ Φῆστος δὲ θέλων τοῖς Ἰουδαίοις χάριν καταθέσθαι ἀποκριθεὶς τῷ Παύλῳ εἶπεν Θέλεις εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα ἀναβὰς ἐκεῖ περὶ τούτων κριθῆναι ἐπ’ ἐμοῦ

passages.text: Paul replied, “I am standing before the judgment seat of Caesar, where I ought to be tried. I have done nothing wrong to the Jews, as you yourself know very well.
passages.sermon:
Paul was a Christian apostle.
Paul stood before Festus, the Roman governor.
Paul spoke to Festus.
Paul said, "I am now standing before Caesar's judgment seat."
"This is the place where I should be judged."
"I have done nothing wrong to the Jews."
"You, Festus, know this very well."
passages.original: Εἶπεν δὲ ὁ Παῦλος Ἑστὼς ἐπὶ τοῦ βήματος Καίσαρος εἰμι οὗ με δεῖ κρίνεσθαι Ἰουδαίους οὐδὲν ἠδίκησα ὡς καὶ σὺ κάλλιον ἐπιγινώσκεις

passages.text: If, however, I am guilty of anything worthy of death, I do not refuse to die. But if there is no truth to their accusations against me, no one has the right to hand me over to them. I appeal to Caesar!”
passages.sermon:
Paul was a Christian apostle.
Paul stood on trial before Festus.
Paul spoke about the charges against him.
Paul said, "If I have done wrong, I accept the consequences."
"If I have committed a crime deserving death, I do not refuse to die."
"But if their accusations are false, no one can hand me over to them."
"I appeal to Caesar."
passages.original: εἰ μὲν οὖν ἀδικῶ καὶ ἄξιον θανάτου πέπραχά τι οὐ παραιτοῦμαι τὸ ἀποθανεῖν εἰ δὲ οὐδέν ἐστιν ὧν οὗτοι κατηγοροῦσίν μου οὐδείς με δύναται αὐτοῖς χαρίσασθαι Καίσαρα ἐπικαλοῦμαι

passages.text: Then Festus conferred with his council and replied, “You have appealed to Caesar. To Caesar you will go!”
passages.sermon:
Festus was the Roman governor.
Festus spoke with his council.
Festus gave his answer.
Festus said, “You have appealed to Caesar.
You will go to Caesar.”
passages.original: Τότε ὁ Φῆστος συλλαλήσας μετὰ τοῦ συμβουλίου ἀπεκρίθη Καίσαρα ἐπικέκλησαι ἐπὶ Καίσαρα πορεύσῃ

passages.text: After several days had passed, King Agrippa and Bernice came down to Caesarea to pay their respects to Festus.
passages.sermon:
King Agrippa was a ruler.
Bernice was with him.
Several days passed.
King Agrippa and Bernice traveled to Caesarea.
They came to see Festus.
They paid their respects to Festus.
passages.original: Ἡμερῶν δὲ διαγενομένων τινῶν Ἀγρίππας ὁ βασιλεὺς καὶ Βερνίκη κατήντησαν εἰς Καισάρειαν ἀσπασάμενοι τὸν Φῆστον

passages.text: Since they were staying several days, Festus laid out Paul’s case before the king: “There is a certain man whom Felix left in prison.
passages.sermon:
King Agrippa and Bernice stayed in Caesarea for several days.
Festus was the Roman governor.
Festus spoke to King Agrippa about Paul.
Festus explained Paul's situation to the king.
Festus said, "There is a man in prison."
Felix, the previous governor, left this man in prison.
This man is Paul.
passages.original: ὡς δὲ πλείους ἡμέρας διέτριβον ἐκεῖ ὁ Φῆστος τῷ βασιλεῖ ἀνέθετο τὰ κατὰ τὸν Παῦλον λέγων Ἀνήρ τίς ἐστιν καταλελειμμένος ὑπὸ Φήλικος δέσμιος

passages.text: While I was in Jerusalem, the chief priests and elders of the Jews presented their case and requested a judgment against him.
passages.sermon:
I was in Jerusalem.
The chief priests of the Jews were there.
The elders of the Jews were there.
They presented their case to me.
They asked me to judge against this man.
passages.original: περὶ οὗ γενομένου μου εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα ἐνεφάνισαν οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ οἱ πρεσβύτεροι τῶν Ἰουδαίων αἰτούμενοι κατ’ αὐτοῦ καταδίκην

passages.text: I told them that it is not the Roman custom to hand a man over before he has had an opportunity to face his accusers and defend himself against their charges.
passages.sermon:
Festus was a Roman governor.
Festus spoke to the Jewish leaders.
Festus told them about Roman law.
Romans do not hand over a person before a trial.
The accused must meet his accusers face to face.
The accused must have a chance to defend himself against the charges.
passages.original: πρὸς οὓς ἀπεκρίθην ὅτι οὐκ ἔστιν ἔθος Ῥωμαίοις χαρίζεσθαί τινα ἄνθρωπον πρὶν ἢ ὁ κατηγορούμενος κατὰ πρόσωπον ἔχοι τοὺς κατηγόρους τόπον τε ἀπολογίας λάβοι περὶ τοῦ ἐγκλήματος

passages.text: So when they came here with me, I did not delay. The next day I sat on the judgment seat and ordered that the man be brought in.
passages.sermon:
The chief priests and elders of the Jews came here with me.
I did not delay.
The next day I sat on the judgment seat.
I ordered that the man be brought in.
passages.original: Συνελθόντων οὖν αὐτῶν ἐνθάδε ἀναβολὴν μηδεμίαν ποιησάμενος τῇ ἑξῆς καθίσας ἐπὶ τοῦ βήματος ἐκέλευσα ἀχθῆναι τὸν ἄνδρα

passages.text: But when his accusers rose to speak, they did not charge him with any of the crimes I had expected.
passages.sermon:
Paul stood before his accusers.
The accusers spoke against Paul.
They did not bring any charges I expected.
I had expected them to accuse Paul of serious crimes.
They did not accuse him of these things.
passages.original: περὶ οὗ σταθέντες οἱ κατήγοροι οὐδεμίαν αἰτίαν ἔφερον ὧν ἐγὼ ὑπενόουν πονηρῶν

passages.text: They only had some contentions with him regarding their own religion and a certain Jesus who had died, but whom Paul affirmed to be alive.
passages.sermon:
Paul stood before his accusers.
His accusers argued with him.
They argued about their own religion.
They also argued about a man named Jesus.
Jesus had died.
Paul said that Jesus was alive.
passages.original: ζητήματα δέ τινα περὶ τῆς ἰδίας δεισιδαιμονίας εἶχον πρὸς αὐτὸν καὶ περί τινος Ἰησοῦ τεθνηκότος ὃν ἔφασκεν ὁ Παῦλος ζῆν

passages.text: Since I was at a loss as to how to investigate these matters, I asked if he was willing to go to Jerusalem and be tried there on these charges.
passages.sermon:
Festus was the Roman governor.
Festus did not know how to investigate these matters.
Festus asked Paul a question.
Festus asked if Paul was willing to go to Jerusalem.
Festus asked if Paul wanted to be tried there on these charges.
passages.original: Ἀπορούμενος δὲ ἐγὼ τὴν περὶ τούτων ζήτησιν ἔλεγον εἰ βούλοιτο πορεύεσθαι εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα κἀκεῖ κρίνεσθαι περὶ τούτων

passages.text: But when Paul appealed to be held over for the decision of the Emperor, I ordered that he be held until I could send him to Caesar.”
passages.sermon:
Paul was a prisoner.
Paul asked to have his case decided by the Emperor.
I gave an order.
I ordered that Paul be kept in custody.
He would remain in custody until I could send him to Caesar.
passages.original: τοῦ δὲ Παύλου ἐπικαλεσαμένου τηρηθῆναι αὐτὸν εἰς τὴν τοῦ Σεβαστοῦ διάγνωσιν ἐκέλευσα τηρεῖσθαι αὐτὸν ἕως οὗ ἀναπέμψω αὐτὸν πρὸς Καίσαρα

passages.text: Then Agrippa said to Festus, “I would like to hear this man myself.” “Tomorrow you will hear him,” Festus declared.
passages.sermon:
King Agrippa spoke to Festus.
Agrippa said he wanted to hear Paul himself.
Festus answered Agrippa.
Festus said Agrippa would hear Paul the next day.
passages.original: Ἀγρίππας δὲ πρὸς τὸν Φῆστον Ἐβουλόμην καὶ αὐτὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἀκοῦσαι Αὔριον φησίν Ἀκούσῃ αὐτοῦ

passages.text: The next day Agrippa and Bernice came with great pomp and entered the auditorium, along with the commanders and leading men of the city. And Festus ordered that Paul be brought in.
passages.sermon:
King Agrippa was a ruler.
Bernice was with him.
The next day, Agrippa and Bernice arrived.
They came with great pomp.
They entered the auditorium.
The commanders of the city came with them.
The leading men of the city also came with them.
Festus was the Roman governor.
Festus gave an order.
The guards brought Paul into the auditorium.
passages.original: Τῇ οὖν ἐπαύριον ἐλθόντος τοῦ Ἀγρίππα καὶ τῆς Βερνίκης μετὰ πολλῆς φαντασίας καὶ εἰσελθόντων εἰς τὸ ἀκροατήριον σύν τε χιλιάρχοις καὶ ἀνδράσιν τοῖς κατ’ ἐξοχὴν τῆς πόλεως καὶ κελεύσαντος τοῦ Φήστου ἤχθη ὁ Παῦλος

passages.text: Then Festus said, “King Agrippa and all who are present with us, you see this man. The whole Jewish community has petitioned me about him, both here and in Jerusalem, crying out that he ought not to live any longer.
passages.sermon:
Festus was the Roman governor.
Agrippa was the king.
Festus spoke to King Agrippa.
Festus also spoke to all the men present with them.
Festus said, “You see this man.”
Festus referred to Paul.
The whole Jewish community spoke to Festus about Paul.
The Jews in Jerusalem spoke to Festus about Paul.
The Jews here also spoke to Festus about Paul.
They all cried out against Paul.
They said Paul should not live any longer.
passages.original: Καί φησιν ὁ Φῆστος Ἀγρίππα βασιλεῦ καὶ πάντες οἱ συμπαρόντες ἡμῖν ἄνδρες θεωρεῖτε τοῦτον περὶ οὗ ἅπαν τὸ πλῆθος τῶν Ἰουδαίων ἐνέτυχόν μοι ἔν τε Ἱεροσολύμοις καὶ ἐνθάδε βοῶντες μὴ δεῖν αὐτὸν ζῆν μηκέτι

passages.text: But I found he had done nothing worthy of death, and since he has now appealed to the Emperor, I decided to send him.
passages.sermon:
Festus was the Roman governor.
Festus examined Paul’s case.
Festus found that Paul had done nothing deserving death.
Paul appealed to the Emperor.
Festus decided to send Paul to the Emperor.
passages.original: ἐγὼ δὲ κατελαβόμην μηδὲν ἄξιον αὐτὸν θανάτου πεπραχέναι αὐτοῦ δὲ τούτου ἐπικαλεσαμένου τὸν Σεβαστὸν ἔκρινα πέμπειν

passages.text: I have nothing definite to write to our sovereign one about him. Therefore I have brought him before all of you, and especially before you, King Agrippa, so that after this inquiry I may have something to write.
passages.sermon:
Festus is the Roman governor.  
Festus speaks to King Agrippa and to everyone present.  
Festus says he does not have anything definite to write about Paul to the emperor.  
Festus brought Paul before all of them.  
Festus especially brought Paul before King Agrippa.  
Festus wants to have this inquiry.  
Festus hopes that after the inquiry, he will have something to write about Paul.
passages.original: περὶ οὗ ἀσφαλές τι γράψαι τῷ κυρίῳ οὐκ ἔχω διὸ προήγαγον αὐτὸν ἐφ’ ὑμῶν καὶ μάλιστα ἐπὶ σοῦ βασιλεῦ Ἀγρίππα ὅπως τῆς ἀνακρίσεως γενομένης σχῶ τί γράψω

passages.text: For it seems unreasonable to me to send on a prisoner without specifying the charges against him.”
passages.sermon:
I am the speaker.
I must send a prisoner.
I think it is unreasonable to send a prisoner.
I must also specify the charges against him.
It does not make sense to send a prisoner without stating the charges.
passages.original: ἄλογον γάρ μοι δοκεῖ πέμποντα δέσμιον μὴ καὶ τὰς κατ’ αὐτοῦ αἰτίας σημᾶναι
